text:
Summary
Data source overview: The Berryville Institute of Machine Learning (BIML) report performs an architectural risk analysis of generic ML systems. It enumerates 78 concrete risks, maps them to nine ML components and system-wide issues, and lists engineering “controls” and classical security principles intended to mitigate those risks.

Inference strategy justification: The report rarely gives end-to-end causal chains in one place; instead risks and suggested controls are scattered. I therefore (1) grouped closely-related risks and controls, (2) reconstructed the implicit reasoning that links each risk to a family of controls, (3) instantiated one representative causal-interventional path for six high-impact risks explicitly highlighted by BIML, and (4) inserted the overarching “defense-in-depth security principle for ML system design” node (explicitly discussed in Part Two) to inter-connect all paths into one fabric.

Extraction completeness explanation: 43 nodes (37 concepts, 6 interventions) and 61 edges cover:
• Six of BIML’s top-ten risks that have the clearest, actionable controls (adversarial examples, data poisoning, privacy leakage, Trojan models, online drift, over-fitting).  
• The full reasoning ladder risk → problem analysis → theoretical insight → design rationale → implementation mechanism → validation evidence → intervention for each.  
• Shared nodes and cross-edges guarantee one connected fabric.

Key limitations:  
• BIML supplies many more minor risks; including all would exceed node budget.  
• Validation evidence is summarised from multiple cited studies rather than original experimental data inside BIML, so evidence confidence is marked ≤4.  
• Some theoretical causes (e.g. “linearity in high-dimensional space”) are mildly inferred from the text (confidence 2).

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[78]

Instruction-set improvement suggestion: Ask the extractor to state which specific paragraphs grounded each node to simplify downstream auditing; this avoids manual hunting through long documents.
